newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sells off over 60 pct of miller.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sells off over 60 pct of miller.

text.p: The Egyptian state sold off 60.75 percent of East Delta Flour Mills, the second company in the strategic sector to leave state control, after the flotation was 30 times oversubscribed, the agents said on Saturday.

The Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills allocated a total of 3,044,860 shares, or 50.75 percent, of East Delta's equity for individuals, mutual funds and financial firms, Mohamed el-Sharnoubi of agents Banque Misr told Reuters.
The firm's employees got the traditional 10 percent, or 600,000 shares.
The company has earlier said it was offering at least 2.4 million shares, or 40 percent of the equity, at a fixed price of 31 pounds a share.
Individual investors got 2,444,860 shares against 1.2 million as originally announced. They applied to buy 37.49 million shares.
Mutual funds and financial institutions got their original allocation of 600,000 shares, despite applying to buy 21.31 million shares.
East Delta manufactures bread and pasta for distribution in eastern provinces.
The firm increased net profits for the 1995/96 financial year which ended on June 30, 1996 to 27.78 million pounds from 27.66 million a year earlier.
The state regards milling firms as strategic and once said it would not sell more than 40 percent of its stake in them.
But heavy demand for an earlier privatisation, Central and West Delta Flour Mills, persuaded it to change its mind.
